1.5.rationale: The Indonesian text defines violence against children to include "penelantaran" (neglect) (Pasal 39), but for women the regulation consistently discusses "kekerasan" against women without defining it to include economic abuse/neglect. The retrieved passages for 1.5 (e.g., Pasal 48 on economic empowerment for women victims) describe post-violence economic recovery measures (training, capital, marketing) and separately mention protection from "eksploitasi ekonomi dan seksual" as a right (Pasal 10(e)), but they do not frame economic exploitation/abuse as a form of violence (kekerasan) itself. Given the source text, answering "No" to an indicator specifically about economic violence is reasonable; thus the golden label "Yes" likely over-interprets empowerment/exploitation language as economic violence.
